newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds look to next wk for chunky dollar deals.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds look to next wk for chunky dollar deals.

text.p: The quiet primary market said the general focus was on next week with Friday's U.S. jobs data putting a dampner on supply.
There was talk of triple-A borrowers tapping the 10-year dollar sector with the Asian Development Bank mooted for a $1.0 billion 10-year global bond, although no mandate had yet been awarded.
Dealers said the European Investment Bank, Fannie Mae and World Bank were also possible candidates.
Thailand is expected to kick off on a roadshow for its dollar deal next week, traders said.
The only chunky deal to surface on Thursday was a 200 million stg 10-year offering for ASDA Group via joint lead managers Merrill Lynch and NatWest Markets.
The bond will be priced later today to yield 65 b.p. over gilts.
"The deal is aimed at UK institutional investors but we've seen good continental demand," a syndicate official at Merrill said. "The market is starved on UK corporate names."
ASDA is also considering a buyback of its 10.875 percent 2010 bonds.
